text:
Alex: Thinking out loud — we should split the inference adapter layer out of the runtime binary and make it a standalone service. Long-term this reduces release blast radius and lets infra teams iterate on transport + auth separately.

Maya: +1. Can you sketch the boundary you have in mind? Is this just HTTP adapters (rest/stream) or also model-specific shims?

Alex: Prototype idea: 3 components — Adapter service (transport, auth, rate-limit), Gateway (routing & policy), Runtime (model execution + KV cache). Adapter<->Gateway uses protobuf/gRPC, Gateway<->Runtime uses internal binary protocol we already have. Adapter is language-agnostic.

Tony: Concern: latency for small requests if we add a network hop. Any thoughts on p99 impact?

Alex: Good call. Expect +1-3ms p50, +5-12ms p99 depending on colocations. Mitigations: colocate adapter on same AZ, keep in-process fast-path for high-QPS customers (sidecar), and use unix sockets for private deployments.

Sasha: What about auth and tenant scoping? We currently do tenant checks in-runtime. Moving to adapter would require us to push tenant metadata through. Risk: client code relying on runtime exceptions.

Alex: Plan is to perform auth & basic quota in Adapter, propagate a signed tenant header to Gateway/Runtime. Runtime retains final authorization layer for policy enforcement. We'll add an idempotent header: x-rw-tenant-proof.

Li: How do we handle KV cache locality? If runtime owns cache, adapter misses go network hop. Could adapter implement a tiny LRU prefix cache for hot prefixes?

Maya: Small prefix cache sgtm. Also add a cache-staleness header so runtime can return cache hints.

Tony: Migration strategy please — we can't do a big-bang.

Alex: Staged rollout: (1) Extract adapter code into a library module + tests, (2) Run adapter packaged as sidecar colocated with runtime (same pod) — zero-net-hop, (3) Sidecar becomes separate service in some AZs, run canary, (4) Enable unix-socket fast-path for private, (5) Default adapter service globally. Each stage gated by perf/compat tests.

Sasha: Tests — add a compatibility matrix: prompt/streaming/kv/stop-sequences/func-calls. Also load tests for batching behavior. File a regression-suite task `ENG-7891`?

Alex: Already created ENG-7891 for compatibility suite and ENG-7892 for infra rollout automation.

Maya: Ownership? Who's owning the adapter extraction RFC and followups?

Alex: I'll drive the RFC. Tony + Li for perf & cache design. Sasha for security & auth. Maya for compatibility tests.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New RFC created: rfc/2025-02-inference-adapter-split.md (link: https://go/rfcs/2025-02-inference-adapter-split) :white_check_mark:

Tony: One last tradeoff — splitting helps iter velocity but increases operational surface area (more services to monitor). Need clear SLO/alerting baked into the plan.

Alex: Agreed. I'll add SLOs to the RFC draft: adapter p95<20ms, error rate <0.05%, and end-to-end p99 budget. We'll also add distributed tracing hooks.

Maya: OK — let's review RFC in next architecture sync. Can you post the draft by EOD Thursday?

Alex: Will do. I'll paste the draft link here when ready.

Li: If you want someone to run microbenchmarks early, ping me and I'll spin up a small rig.

Sasha: Assigning follow-ups: ENG-7891 (compat suite), ENG-7892 (rollout infra), ENG-7893 (adapter library extraction).

Tony: 👍

Alex: Thanks all. Short doc + migration checklist will be in the RFC. Expect an initial perf spreadsheet in 48hrs.
